entries.raw: **[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
entries.text: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)

entries.raw: *Teams of militants assaulted the [[Afghan army]] in the north of the country and in the capital, killing at least 16 members of the security forces. [https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2010/12/18/world/asia/AP-AS-Afghanistan.html?_r=1&hp (The New York Times)] [http://news.xinhuanet.com/english2010/world/2010-12/19/c_13655863.htm (Xinhua)]
entries.text: Teams of militants assaulted the Afghan army in the north of the country and in the capital, killing at least 16 members of the security forces.

entries.raw: *An [[Israel]]i air-strike in the [[Gaza Strip]] kills five [[Palestinian political violence|Palestinian militants]] according to Palestinian sources; Israel says they were attempting to [[Palestinian rocket attacks on Israel|fire missiles]] into [[Israel]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-12029802 (BBC)][http://www.cnn.com/2010/WORLD/meast/12/18/gaza.israel.strike/ (CNN)][http://www.jpost.com/Defense/Article.aspx?id=200036 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
entries.text: An Israeli air-strike in the Gaza Strip kills five Palestinian militants according to Palestinian sources; Israel says they were attempting to fire missiles into Israel.

entries.raw: *The [[United States]]' [[unemployment rate]] rises in 21 states, the highest number to report an increase since August. It falls in 15 states. [http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2010/dec/17/unemployment-rate-rises-21-states-falls-15/ (''Washington Times'')]
entries.text: The United States' unemployment rate rises in 21 states, the highest number to report an increase since August. It falls in 15 states.

entries.raw: *[[Bank of America]] bans [[Wikileaks]] payments as a result of news of an upcoming release of information on banks in the United States that could leave an impact. [http://www.nypost.com/p/news/international/bank_of_america_refuses_wikileaks_SgH3pnkKzKm3Y2Li48s6XL (''New York Post'')]
entries.text: Bank of America bans Wikileaks payments as a result of news of an upcoming release of information on banks in the United States that could leave an impact.

entries.raw: *At least 30 people drown after a boat capsizes in northeastern [[Bangladesh]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-south-asia-12029183 (BBC)] [http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/south-asia/35-feared-dead-in-Bangladesh-boat-accident-Official-/articleshow/7125265.cms (''Times of India'')]
entries.text: At least 30 people drown after a boat capsizes in northeastern Bangladesh.

entries.raw: *A [[People's Republic of China|Chinese]] fishing boat capsizes during a scuffle with a [[South Korea]]n coastguard ship, leaving one dead and two missing. [http://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5ibO9E4jBOaNVFyk-LI_TCCQbRDBg?docId=8ad015587c064618aa95f973b1a6fa8d (AP)] [http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/afp_asiapacific/view/1099944/1/.html (Channel News Asia)]
entries.text: A Chinese fishing boat capsizes during a scuffle with a South Korean coastguard ship, leaving one dead and two missing.

links.raw: [[Winter of 2010-2011 in Great Britain and Ireland|heavy snowfall]]
links.target: Winter of 2010-2011 in Great Britain and Ireland

entries.raw: *Roads, railways and airports across the [[United Kingdom]] are severely affected by further [[Winter of 2010-2011 in Great Britain and Ireland|heavy snowfall]]. Severe weather warnings have been issued for many areas. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-12025538 (BBC)]
entries.text: Roads, railways and airports across the United Kingdom are severely affected by further heavy snowfall. Severe weather warnings have been issued for many areas.

entries.raw: *[[Ivory Coast]] crisis:
entries.text: Ivory Coast crisis:

links.raw: [[List of heads of state of Côte d'Ivoire|President]]
links.target: List of heads of state of Côte d'Ivoire

entries.raw: **[[Kenya]] calls on [[Africa]]n nations to oust [[Ivory Coast]] incumbent [[List of heads of state of Côte d'Ivoire|President]] [[Laurent Gbagbo]] from office, by force if necessary, if he does not step down. [http://english.aljazeera.net/news/africa/2010/12/201012188402027780.html (Al Jazeera)]
entries.text: Kenya calls on African nations to oust Ivory Coast incumbent President Laurent Gbagbo from office, by force if necessary, if he does not step down.

links.target: United Nations Operation in Côte d'Ivoire

entries.raw: **Incumbent President Laurent Gbagbo orders [[United Nations]] [[United Nations Operation in Côte d'Ivoire|peacekeepers]] to leave the country. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-12028263 (BBC)]
entries.text: Incumbent President Laurent Gbagbo orders United Nations peacekeepers to leave the country.

links.raw: [[Republic of Korea Armed Forces|South Korean military]]

entries.raw: *[[Republic of Korea Armed Forces|South Korean military]] officials say they will proceed with planned live-fire artillery drills from an [[Bombardment of Yeonpyeong|island bombarded]] by  [[North Korea]] last month, despite threats of retaliation. [https://web.archive.org/web/20101222011145/http://www.voanews.com/english/news/South-Korea-to-Go-Ahead-with-Live-Fire-Drills---112121084.html (VOA)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-pacific-12029875 (BBC)]
entries.text: South Korean military officials say they will proceed with planned live-fire artillery drills from an island bombarded by North Korea last month, despite threats of retaliation.

links.raw: [[Premier of the People's Republic of China|Premier]]
links.target: Premier of the People's Republic of China

entries.raw: *[[People's Republic of China|Chinese]] [[Premier of the People's Republic of China|Premier]] [[Wen Jiabao]] arrives for a working visit in [[Pakistan]] and meets with [[Prime Minister of Pakistan|Pakistani Prime Minister]] [[Yusuf Raza Gilani]]. [http://www.thehindu.com/news/article959171.ece (''The Hindu'')]
entries.text: Chinese Premier Wen Jiabao arrives for a working visit in Pakistan and meets with Pakistani Prime Minister Yusuf Raza Gilani.

entries.raw: *Palestinian Prime Minister [[Salam Fayyad]] says that there has been a change in the Palestinian mindset and they "are fully committed to non-violence". [http://www.jpost.com/MiddleEast/Article.aspx?id=200004 (''Jerusalem Post'')]
entries.text: Palestinian Prime Minister Salam Fayyad says that there has been a change in the Palestinian mindset and they "are fully committed to non-violence".

links.raw: [[2010 Eocheong boat collision incident|incident near Eocheong island]]

entries.raw: *A PRC fishing boat collided with a South Korea coastguard ship causing an [[2010 Eocheong boat collision incident|incident near Eocheong island]] [https://news.yahoo.com/s/afp/20101218/wl_afp/skoreachinaaccidentsea_20101218132055 (''Yahoo'')]
entries.text: A PRC fishing boat collided with a South Korea coastguard ship causing an incident near Eocheong island

entries.raw: *[[Nigeria]] agrees to drop corruption charges against [[Dick Cheney]] and [[Halliburton]] in exchange for a $250 million [[Settlement (litigation)|settlement]]. [http://www.businessweek.com/news/2010-12-17/nigeria-withdraws-charges-against-cheney-halliburton.html (Business Week)]
entries.text: Nigeria agrees to drop corruption charges against Dick Cheney and Halliburton in exchange for a $250 million settlement.

entries.raw: *Hundreds of people, including nationalists, are arrested in the [[Russia]]n capital [[Moscow]] in an attempt to prevent an outbreak of ethnic violence. [https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSTRE6BH1FX20101218 (Reuters)] [http://en.rian.ru/russia/20101218/161834478.html (RIA Novosti)]
entries.text: Hundreds of people, including nationalists, are arrested in the Russian capital Moscow in an attempt to prevent an outbreak of ethnic violence.

entries.raw: *Around 140 prisoners break out of jail in [[Nuevo Laredo]], northern [[Mexico]]. [http://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2010/12/18/140-inmates-escape-Mexican-prison/UPI-97241292650513/ (UPI)]
entries.text: Around 140 prisoners break out of jail in Nuevo Laredo, northern Mexico.

entries.raw: *The [[United States Senate]] repeals "[[Don't Ask Don't Tell]]" by a vote of 65-35. The bill will now be sent to President [[Barack Obama]] to be signed. [https://www.nytimes.com/2010/12/19/us/politics/19cong.html?_r=1&hp (New York Times)]
entries.text: The United States Senate repeals "Don't Ask Don't Tell" by a vote of 65-35. The bill will now be sent to President Barack Obama to be signed.

entries.raw: *An [[Italy|Italian]] court grants [[Amanda Knox]] a review of the forensic evidence used to convict her of the 2007 murder of British student Meredith Kercher. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-12025862 (BBC)]
entries.text: An Italian court grants Amanda Knox a review of the forensic evidence used to convict her of the 2007 murder of British student Meredith Kercher.

entries.raw: *The [[Venezuela]]n parliament temporarily grants more powers to [[List of Presidents of Venezuela|President]] [[Hugo Chávez]] in the wake of recent flooding, allowing him to pass laws by [[decree]] without the support of the [[National Assembly of Venezuela|National Assembly]].[https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-12024935 (BBC)]
entries.text: The Venezuelan parliament temporarily grants more powers to President Hugo Chávez in the wake of recent flooding, allowing him to pass laws by decree without the support of the National Assembly.
